title: Safe transactional adapter for Optimize recommendations API + webhook-driven rollout
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Build a small, production-ready transactional adapter and SDK primitives that let Optimize generate batching/caching recommendations and safely apply or rollback configuration changes via API + webhook-driven workflows. The adapter should enforce idempotent applies, provide a clear rollback path (compensating actions), and expose observability hooks so Console + SRE can monitor, trace, and reason about partial failures.

Motivation: Current experiments show surface-level recommendations can be generated, but applying them to runtime config is brittle: double-applies, race conditions during concurrent plan execution, and lack of deterministic rollback cause outages or manual intervention. We need an API/SDK pattern that is developer-friendly for customers of Redwood Optimize and safe for platform automation (canary rollouts, retries, and automated revert).

High-level approach: implement a light 'saga-style' operation resource that moves through plan -> pre-validate -> reserve -> apply -> confirm phases. Each operation is identified by an operation_id (idempotency token) provided by the caller (SDK or automation). The control-plane records operation state and last-applied diff; apply requests are guarded by lease-based locks and implement compensating operations for rollback. Webhooks are emitted for each state transition with a stable event id and backoff-friendly retry semantics.

API sketch (proposal):
- POST /v1/optimize/operations (body: plan, candidate_changes, operation_id) => returns operation resource with status=planned
- POST /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id}/reserve => attempts to acquire apply reservation; returns 200 if reserved or 409 if another active reservation exists
- POST /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id}/apply (idempotent) => performs the apply; requires operation_id and client nonce; supports dry_run flag
- POST /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id}/rollback => triggers compensating actions based on recorded diff
- GET /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id} => status + audit trail

Webhook events: op_planned, op_reserved, op_apply_started, op_applied, op_apply_failed, op_rolled_back. Each webhook includes operation_id, event_id, timestamp, last_known_state, and a small stable diff payload for observers. Webhook delivery respects exponential backoff and a configurable dead-letter policy (DLQ S3/bucket + manual inspection link).

SDK primitives: OptClient.createOperation(plan, {operationId}), OptClient.reserveOperation(operationId), OptClient.applyOperation(operationId, {idempotencyNonce, dryRun}), OptClient.rollbackOperation(operationId), OptClient.watchEvents(operationId, handler). SDK will auto-generate operation IDs when not supplied, but callers are encouraged to pass deterministic operation IDs for retries from automation.

Observability and safety: every operation logs a single trace that spans planning through apply/rollback; metrics include apply_success, apply_conflict, rollback_initiated, rollback_success, and time_to_settle. Token-level cost delta and estimated token-savings are attached to the operation for Console reporting.

Acceptance criteria and rollout gating below.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints implemented and documented in OpenAPI spec with examples for idempotent apply and rollback
SDK primitives exist for Node + Python and include automatic idempotency token generation and retry helpers
Server persists operation state and recorded diff; repeated POST /apply with same operation_id is a no-op after success and returns 200 with final state
Concurrent reserve attempts are deterministic (one winner) and returning 409 for losers; recorded in metrics
End-to-end integration test that simulates concurrent planners and ensures exactly-once net effect for a sample workload
Webhook delivery with exponential backoff and DLQ behavior validated in staging; Console shows event timeline
Canary rollout plan (internal first, 10% customers, then global) with rollback playbook validated
Tracing and cost-metrics are visible in Console for at least 30 days in staging and 7 days in production at rollout
Security review completed for API surface and webhook signing; KMS used for DLQ access control if storing diffs
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed to saga-ish operation resource; prefer lease-based reservation over DB-level locks to reduce contention. Action: write API contract and OpenAPI draft.
2025-02-18 Liam Chen: Posted OpenAPI draft in design_links. Initial SDK wireframes (Node/Python) attached. Need SRE review for DLQ/visibility.
2025-02-22 Rajan Iyer (SRE): Feedback — ensure webhook retries use jitter and provide a non-destructive idempotency header. Also suggested adding a max-lifetime lease to avoid orphaned reservations.

2025-02-25 Sofia Martinez (Product): Updated acceptance criteria to include cost delta reporting and Console timeline. Suggested that canary expose a toggle in Console to pause applies per-organization.

2025-03-01 Liam Chen: Implemented server-side persistence and basic apply handler. Manual test: double-apply with same operation_id returned 200 and did not duplicate config changes. Pushed WIP PR: pr_links[0].

2025-03-04 Maya Patel: Code review notes — add integration test simulating concurrent reserve+apply and add tracing instrumentation across services. Also, add signed webhook payloads for consumer verification.
notes: Risk: Compensating rollback is necessarily best-effort for external systems; ensure manual rollback path and operator runbook are ready before global rollout.
Migration: existing ad-hoc apply endpoints will be deprecated after 2 weeks of canary and replaced by the operation API. Provide compatibility shim in SDK.
Next steps: complete SDK error semantics, finalize DLQ storage path with security, write runbook and incident playbook, schedule canary 2025-03-18.
